groups.sentence: Instructors design courses so AI cannot stand in for the thinking students must perform themselves.
Instructors tell students that AI is a tool that supports learning and does not substitute for their thinking.
Students use AI to support and enhance, not replace, their learning, thinking and own work.
Students must not use AI to replace or bypass their own thinking, analysis, effort or the learning an assignment builds.
Students must be the primary author, and the ideas, analysis and final work must be their own.
Students do not rely solely on AI output, and treat it as a starting point to evaluate and build on.
Students ask themselves whether their AI use helps them learn or replaces their own work, and use judgment.
Everyone must keep human judgment in the loop and not rely solely on AI for decisions.
Students make their final submission show how they developed and refined ideas and directed AI with their own critical thinking.
Students must not use AI summaries in place of doing the reading themselves.
AI is not a substitute for human thinking, judgment, creativity or learning.
Everyone should use AI to augment, not replace, human judgment, thinking, creativity and learning.
AI use must support learning, and the intellectual effort and ownership must remain with the person.
Instructors use AI as a supplement to teaching and expertise, not a replacement for human interaction or faculty knowledge.
